_source: 2300AD Core Book 1, chargen extract, printed p14 (pdf 8).
_replaces: The Traveller Core Rulebook's eight skill packages entirely. 2300AD supplies five of its own and none of the Traveller names carry over.
_rule: Used after ALL Travellers have been created -- still a group rule, as in Traveller, so the generator should present the package and let the player tick what they claimed rather than granting the lot.

Troubleshooter.desc: For a group of experienced professionals who solve problems for a corporation, government agency or other organisation.

Colonist.desc: For a campaign where the Travellers must survive the harsh challenges of a frontier world.

Urbanite.desc: For Travellers working the streets of a technologically advanced but decadent urban environment.

Libertine Trader.desc: Suits a group of free traders, plying the spaceways between colonies and avoiding the Core.

Corporate.desc: For a group that largely works in a corporate environment, whether in the Core or on the Frontier.

_TRANSCRIPTION_NOTES: Urbanite lists 'Melee (any)' with NO level where every other entry in every package carries a 1. Transcribed as printed. Almost certainly means Melee (any) 1 -- but under the Traveller skill rules an entry with no level listed means 'gain at 1 if untrained, else +1', which is a genuinely different and slightly better outcome, so it is left as printed rather than normalised.
Libertine Trader says 'Engineering 1'. The skill is called ENGINEER everywhere else in Traveller and in 2300AD's own skill-changes list. Recorded as printed; treat as Engineer when resolving.
Urbanite says 'Computers 1'. Traveller has no such skill -- it is Electronics (computers). Recorded as printed; treat as Electronics (computers) when resolving.
Package sizes vary: Troubleshooter and Colonist hold 8, Libertine Trader 9, Urbanite and Corporate 7.
